/projects/apriltags.title: Camera Telemetry Stabilization on Drones - Joshua Tarara's Portfolio
p: This project explores using AprilTag-based visual feedback to stabilize a quadcopter drone in 3D space without relying on an IMU. Instead, it estimates the droneâs position from downward-facing camera telemetry and adjusts flight using software PID control.
C++, UNIX, Linux, Python, Apriltags, Pose Estimation

A downward-facing camera identifies AprilTags and estimates relative pose (translation and rotation) of the drone.
Using pose data, a PID controller adjusts motor thrust commands to stabilize the drone directly over the target tag.
No IMU, GPS, or external sensors are usedâcontrol is fully vision-based.

Software:

AprilTag Detection & Pose Estimation
	Language: C++ or Python (using OpenCV + AprilTag library)
	Function: Captures camera feed, detects AprilTags, and computes 6-DOF pose (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw) relative to the tag.
	Output: 3D position and orientation used as control input.

Drone Stabilization Logic
	â¢	Control System: PID controller (Proportional, Integral, Derivative)
	Inputs: Pose estimation errors
	Outputs: Adjusted movement commands or virtual motor thrust (in simulation)

3D Simulation Engine
	â¢	Library: matplotlib with mpl_toolkits.mplot3d
	Features:
	â¢	Real-time 3D visualization of drone and AprilTag
	â¢	Trail line showing drone trajectory
	â¢	Simulated physics with position, velocity, acceleration

Interactive GUI
	â¢	Framework: matplotlib.widgets
	Controls:
	â¢	Sliders for initial drone position and PID gains (Kp, Ki, Kd)
	â¢	âPlayâ button to start/stop simulation
	Purpose: Allows live tuning and intuitive understanding of how PID parameters affect drone behavior

Motion Behavior
	â¢	Spiral Flight Path Generator:
	â¢	Adds a small circular offset to x/y while climbing in z
	â¢	Helps visualize convergence toward target height (1.5 m above tag)

Successfully demonstrated stable hovering using only visual feedback.
Simulation revealed tuning thresholds and controller response behavior.
Provides a scalable foundation for vision-based autonomous drone navigation and landing systems.

/projects/wirebondingfixture.title: Multi-up wire bonding fixture & bracket - Joshua Tarara's Portfolio
p: Designed and fabricated a device that secures and zeros multiple modules to a known offset point in an autobonder to be wire bonded automatically. This was done by carefully defining primary mating surfaces used in the end product (held to a higher tollerence) and by using a mix of springs and pins the components were held in place by constant spring force.
DFM/DFA, Tollerence Stack-ups, ECO process, Solidworks, 3D printing

Performed multiple design reviews to initiate the design process. Followed ECO processes to track product lifecycle. Used DFM/DFA for the milled and 3D printed components using SolidWorks to design the bracket and plate. Exercised Tollerence stack-up reviews on all drawings. Designed in Helicoil inserts to increase torque cycling of mounting screws by 10x to 100x. Used exotic FR-PC-ABS printing filament to ensure temp. resistance durring prototyping.

Increased production for a behind schedule program to increase manufacturing efficiency by 400%.
Worked closely with our in-house machine shop and the manufacturing floor.

/projects/talos.title: TALOS (Thermal Arial Lift Observation System) - Joshua Tarara's Portfolio
p: 4+1 VTOL fixed wing drone that utilizes a 3-axis gimbal thermal/visual fusion camera set to find, locate, and coordinate recovery of low power rocket launches (L1-2). This project arose out of a need from the Florida Tech Panther Rocket Lab to cut down on rocket recover time. The launch area used by the Rocketry team is an overgrown field in West Melbourne, FL - and by locating the rockets after they have flown and possibly drifted, more rockets can be launched in the launch window, and impact on the launch area can be minimized.
Project Management, SCRUM, Agile management, Cross-functional team management
By using a COTS Drone model and COTS electrical components and flight control hardware, the efficentcy of early prototyping was increased on the cost front and workload.
